title: A proof run attestation from the provider's store, with the signing service's trust root of its day
environment: Files only: the test reads them in process, with no network.
records: The bundle that GitHub's attestations API gave on 2026-10-31 for commit 8bcc0d4c853a274bdf33cf80035a0937a6ad03f4: the proof run of pull request 24, signed by proof-run.yml at refs/pull/24/merge, Rekor entry 3614924958. The public-good Sigstore trust root, trusted_root.json from Sigstore's TUF repository on the same day.
prepare: Nothing: the test reads the file.
reset: Nothing: the test changes only copies in memory.
description: Real evidence for the in-process signature check, so the test proves the check against what the provider keeps, not against a fake of it.

title: The coverage output of the pinned spec check for a small product
environment: Files only: the test reads the file in process, with no Lathe.
records: The machine-readable output of lathe check from Lathe 72ab28b6 (schema 5) for the coverage fixture of the coverage tests at its first commit: the domain FX-LEND with three invariants and the product's constraint FX-VO01-C01; 4 obligations, 4 designed, 2 built, 2 proved. Each kind carries its complexity and each coverage scope its debt.
prepare: Nothing: the test reads the file.
description: Real output of the pinned spec check, so the test proves that the coverage reader reads what that version gives, not a fake of it.

title: A fixture registry with three archetypes and one alpha component
environment: Files only: a registry folder and an empty project folder in a temporary folder of the test, with the stego binary built from the commit under test. No network.
records: A local registry copied from registry/ at the commit under test, with the archetypes rest-crud, rpc-service and browser-service and their components and slots. One more component, rh-sso-auth, at stage alpha with the sunset 2099-12-31 and the successor stage beta. A project configuration that names this registry as a local source pinned at its full commit.
prepare: Copy the registry into the temporary folder, commit it, and write the project configuration that pins it.
description: The registry that the checking and scaffold tests read, so that each test knows the archetypes, components, settings and slots it expects.

title: An accepted rest-crud declaration
environment: Files only: the project folder of ST-DECL-TD01, with the stego binary built from the commit under test. No network.
records: ST-DECL-TD01 and the declaration service.yaml: service name todo-svc, archetype rest-crud, base path /api/todo/v1, one entity Todo (tenant omitted, so owned) with the fields title (string, min_length 1, max_length 255) and done (bool, default false), and one collection todos over Todo with create, read, update, delete and list. The entity's id is implicit, because the declaration format has no uuid field type and gives each entity its id. No tenancy, audit, authorization, idempotency, ledger, controller or slot binding is declared. stego validate accepts it.
prepare: Write service.yaml into the project folder of ST-DECL-TD01, and an empty fills folder.
description: The one accepted declaration that most tests change in one named place, so that each fault a test expects comes from that one change.

title: A declaration that binds authorization to a fixture schema
environment: Files only: the project folder of ST-DECL-TD02. No network and no authorization provider.
records: ST-DECL-TD02 with authorization bound: provider spicedb, schema path authz/schema.zed, subject from identity user. The schema defines user, service_account, folder (relation viewer: user) and document (relations owner: user and viewer: user | service_account; permissions view = viewer + owner and edit = owner; caveat ip_allowed with the parameter ip). Todo has the resource type document, the permissions create: edit, read: view, update: edit, delete: edit and list: view, and the relationship owner from the field owner_id with the subject type user. No entity uses the resource type folder. stego validate accepts it.
prepare: Write authz/schema.zed and the authorization settings into the project of ST-DECL-TD02.
description: The accepted authorization declaration that the authorization tests change in one named place.

title: A declaration with a EUR ledger
environment: Files only: the project folder of ST-DECL-TD02. No network.
records: ST-DECL-TD02 and an entity Wallet of kind ledger: currency EUR, transfer codes topup, purchase and refund, two phase yes, pending timeout 15m, snapshot every 3. Its accounts are customer_wallet (normal credit, minimum balance 0 EUR, owner customer, hot no) and settlement (normal debit, hot yes). The collection transfers over Wallet allows create, post, void, reverse, read and list. stego validate accepts it.
prepare: Write the ledger entity and its collection into the declaration of ST-DECL-TD02.
description: The accepted ledger declaration that the money and ledger tests change in one named place.

title: A generated service on a real PostgreSQL, with fake identity and authorization
environment: A PostgreSQL 16 server in a local container without privilege, at a pinned image digest, that the suite starts on the developer workstation or a CI runner, with CPU, memory and time limits (ST-STD-LOCAL). The service is generated from the test's declaration by stego apply and built with the pinned Go SDK. A fake token issuer signs identity tokens, and a fake AuthZEN provider answers decisions and records each call it gets.
accounts: A user u1 in the tenant org-a and a user u2 in the tenant org-b, each with an identity token whose claim org.id names the tenant.
records: An empty database that the generated migrations made. The fake provider holds no relationship.
prepare: Start PostgreSQL and the fakes, run stego apply on the test's declaration, build the service and start it with the modes the test names.
reset: Stop the service, drop the database, and clear the fake provider's records.
description: The running service that the tests of runtime behaviour drive, so that a test sees what the generated code stores, audits and sends, not what a fake of the code claims.

title: Lifecycle records for the digests of the small service's registry
environment: Files only, beside the registry copy of ST-GEN-TD03, read from the registry's current head. Each date is relative to the day T the test runs.
records: Six variants, and each test names the one it writes. Standing: digest DA1 of component A (its digest at R1) is superseded by DA2 (its digest at R2), fails after T+90 days, needs no declaration change and no fill change, advisory ADV-1. Past: the same supersession, failing after T-30 days. Withdrawn: digest DB1 of component B (another component of the active set) is withdrawn with the reason 'leaks a token in a log', fails after T+60 days, advisory ADV-2. Withdrawn past: the same withdrawal, failing after T-10 days. Runtime: the runtime library version V1 that the archetype pins is superseded by V2, fails after T+90 days or, in its past form, after T-30 days, advisory ADV-3. Unreadable: the lifecycle folder holds one record that is not valid.
prepare: Write the records of the variant that the test names into the lifecycle folder of the registry copy, and commit them at the registry's head; the service's registry pin stays at R1.
reset: Delete the lifecycle folder, or the temporary folders of ST-GEN-TD03.
description: The standing of each pin of the small service in each state that matters, so that a test shows what validate, plan and apply do for each, through the binary.

title: Six service checkouts and a registry with two advisories
environment: Files only, in a temporary folder: six service checkouts, each a git repository with one commit, and a registry checkout; no network. Each date is relative to the day T the test runs.
records: alpha pins component A 1.2.0 at digest D1 and component C 2.0.0 at F1. bravo pins A 1.2.0 at D1 and component B 0.9.0 at E1. charlie pins A 1.3.0 at D2 and B 0.9.0 at E1. delta pins C 2.0.0 at F1 only. echo holds generated output under out and no .stego/state.yaml. foxtrot holds a record whose format version is 99. Each record of alpha to delta has format version 2, the first format that names each component digest, and passes stego drift. The registry holds advisory ADV-2, D1 superseded by D2 and failing after T+90 days, and advisory ADV-3, E1 withdrawn with a reason and failing after T+60 days. Each digest is 64 lower-case hexadecimal digits.
prepare: Make the small service of ST-GEN-TD03 with stego apply, copy it into alpha to delta and foxtrot, set the service name and the pins of each copied record (and the format version of foxtrot), copy its output alone into echo, and commit each checkout. Write the two advisories into the lifecycle folder of the registry and commit it.
description: A small fleet in which each service holds a known pin, one checkout has no record and one has a record of an unknown format, so a sweep test can count each answer.

title: A service with a delivery stanza and a fixture registry
environment: A new temporary folder on the developer workstation or a CI runner, with the stego binary built from the commit under test, a copy of the fixture registry and the Go toolchain. No network.
records: A rest-crud declaration for the service orders, with postgres-adapter, a Kafka producer, the SSO JWT verifier and health-check, and a delivery stanza that names the hosted CI provider, the Argo CD project orders and the location of the platform's environment files. Between them, the components state one need of each of the nine requirement kinds: the secret orders-database with the keys url and password, the configuration value LOG_LEVEL, the backing store orders-db, the topic order-events, the identity issuer sso, the ingress http on port 8080, the egress destination payments on port 443, the cluster permission to get config maps, and the pod security level restricted. The fixture registry's ci-pipeline component pins the platform's shared pipeline and the STEGO checks each by a 40-character commit, pins the Konflux standard pipeline bundle and the STEGO checks bundle each by a sha256 digest, and names the keyless identity of the pinned shared pipeline and a Tekton Chains public key as the trusted signers. The registry holds no advisory.
prepare: Copy the fixture service and the fixture registry into a new temporary folder, set STEGO_REGISTRY to the registry copy, then make a Git repository of the service copy and commit it. A test that needs the generated files runs stego apply as its first step.
description: The one service that the Delivering use case tests apply the plan to, so that each test starts from the same declaration, the same component needs and the same ci-pipeline pins.

title: Platform requirements and an environment file that meets them
environment: Files only, in a new temporary folder. No network and no cluster.
records: The platform requirements file that stego apply writes for the service of ST-DLV-TD01, kept as a fixture, and an environment file for the environment dev that meets each requirement: the secret orders-database with the keys url and password, whose values are the canary text CANARY-SECRET-VALUE, the configuration value LOG_LEVEL, the backing store, the topic, the identity issuer, the ingress, the egress destination payments with an address and port 443, the cluster permission, the pod security level, and the image named by a sha256 digest. The environment file holds no value that no requirement names.
prepare: Copy the two files into a new temporary folder and record the hash and the modification time of each file in the folder.
description: The start of each environment check test: a test changes one value of the copy to make the case it checks.

title: Two candidate images of one revision, with their build record
environment: Files, and a local OCI registry that the test starts as a local process on the developer workstation or a CI runner: the TLS registry fixture (scripts/registry-fixture.go), with its guard that asks for CI lifted for a workstation run (ST-STD-LOCAL). No outside network.
records: For one revision of the service of ST-DLV-TD01: the build record that stego build writes and its sha256 digest; an image that stego image build makes from that record, signed with a test key that stands in for the keyless identity of the platform's pinned shared pipeline; and an image that buildah builds from the generated Containerfile with the network off, as the Konflux standard pipeline builds it, signed with a test key that stands in for the Tekton Chains key. Both images are pushed to the local registry with their SPDX and CycloneDX SBOM and provenance referrers. A copy of the fixture registry of ST-DLV-TD01 with no advisory.
prepare: Start the local OCI registry, push the two fixture image layouts with their referrers, and copy the build record and the registry into a new temporary folder.
reset: Stop the local OCI registry, delete its storage, and delete the temporary folder.
description: The candidates that the delivery candidate check tests run on, one from each provider, so that a test shows a result for both providers from one revision.

title: A local stand-in of the hosted CI provider
environment: On the developer workstation (ST-STD-LOCAL): a local Git server that holds the test repository and a copy of the platform's shared pipeline at a known commit; a local runner, at a pinned version in containers without privilege, that runs the provider's workflow format, such as nektos/act; a local keyless signing stand-in that issues a short-lived certificate naming the workflow that the runner ran, at its commit, with a local transparency log; a local attestation store that keeps the provider's attestation API; and the TLS registry fixture as the test image repository. No outside network.
accounts: A test bot account of the local Git server, with write access to the two test repositories and the test image repository only.
records: The service of ST-DLV-TD01 with its generated files, whose ci-pipeline pins name the known commit of the shared pipeline copy.
prepare: Start the local Git server, the runner, the signing stand-in, the attestation store and the registry fixture, then push the service to a new branch of the test repository.
reset: Stop each local service and delete its storage and the temporary folder.
description: Where the tests that need the hosted CI provider run the generated CI file, against a local stand-in that keeps the provider's contract for pipeline runs, signing and attestations. The same tests MAY run again on the real provider, in a test repository with a test bot account, as a second, platform-level proof.

title: A local Konflux stand-in for the test service
environment: On the developer workstation (ST-STD-LOCAL): Tekton Pipelines and Tekton Chains, at pinned versions, in a local kind cluster on rootless Podman, with CPU, memory and time limits. They run the Konflux standard pipeline bundle that the registry pins, from the TLS registry fixture, with hermetic builds and Go module prefetch turned on, and a local Git server that holds the test repository of ST-DLV-TD04.
accounts: A service account that can start pipeline runs and read their results in the test namespace of the kind cluster only.
records: The service of ST-DLV-TD01 with a delivery stanza that names Konflux, and its generated PipelineRun and Containerfile.
prepare: Start the kind cluster, install Tekton Pipelines and Tekton Chains at their pinned versions, push the bundles to the registry fixture, and push the service to a new branch of the test repository, so that a pipeline run starts for it.
reset: Delete the kind cluster, the registry fixture's storage and the temporary folder.
description: Where the tests that need Konflux run the generated PipelineRun, against a local stand-in that runs Konflux's own pinned pipeline bundle, prefetch, hermetic build and Tekton Chains signature. The same tests MAY run again on a real Konflux tenant as a second, platform-level proof.

title: A local GitOps test environment with Argo CD
environment: On the developer workstation (ST-STD-LOCAL): a local kind cluster on rootless Podman, with CPU, memory and time limits, that runs Argo CD at a pinned version, a local Git server that holds the platform's GitOps test repository, and the TLS registry fixture. The kind node container has privilege only inside the user's own user namespace, and no privilege on the host.
accounts: An Argo CD account that can sync applications in the test project only.
records: The service of ST-DLV-TD01 with its generated Kubernetes base and ApplicationSet, its image of ST-DLV-TD03 in the local registry, and in the GitOps repository one environment file and one overlay for the environment test, with the image digest, the namespace orders-test, two replicas and a PodDisruptionBudget.
prepare: Start the kind cluster and install Argo CD at its pinned version, create the test namespace and the Argo CD project orders, push the service and the GitOps repository to the Git server, and push the image.
reset: Delete the kind cluster, the Git repositories, the registry fixture's storage and the temporary folder.
description: Where the tests of deploying with GitOps run, so that Argo CD reads the base, the overlay and the environment files on a real Kubernetes API as it does on the platform. A run in the jshell cluster test namespace MAY follow as a second, platform-level proof.

title: A rest-crud project with one fill at each standing
environment: A new temporary folder on the test host, with the stego binary built from the commit under test, the built-in registry, the Go toolchain with GOPROXY=off over the module cache of the job, and the keys of ST-EXT-TD02. No network.
accounts: The service author, who signs with listed-ssh of ST-EXT-TD02.
records: A project from stego init --archetype rest-crud with the collections org-users and org-groups, and the SIGNERS file of ST-EXT-TD02 at its root. Fills, each for rest-api.before_create and org-users unless named: qualified-fill (current evidence, and a sign-off by listed-ssh); stale-fill (evidence and a sign-off by listed-ssh, then a change of one line in policy.go); unsigned-fill (current evidence, no sign-off); unlisted-fill (current evidence, and a sign-off by unlisted-ssh); untested-fill (code and a passing test, no evidence); untested-fill-2 (code and a passing test for org-groups, no evidence); no-tests-fill (code and no _test.go file); other-slot-fill (current evidence and a sign-off by listed-ssh, for rest-api.before_delete). Each fill's code imports only out/slots and the standard library. service.yaml binds no fill until a test binds one.
prepare: Run stego init in the temporary folder, write the fills from the fixture, run stego test, and run stego fill sign with the key named for each fill that needs a sign-off. Then change one line of policy.go in stale-fill.
reset: Remove the temporary folder. Nothing outside it changes.
description: One fill at each qualification standing and for each reason that a fill is not qualified, so that a test can find the one fill that a check misses, by its name.

title: Test signing keys, listed and not listed
environment: Temporary HOME and GNUPGHOME folders on the test host, with ssh-keygen and gpg on the PATH. No hardware key and no network.
accounts: The service author, as the holder of the keys below; STEGO holds no key.
records: listed-ssh: an ed25519 SSH key pair with no passphrase, set as the signing key in the git config of the test HOME (gpg.format ssh, user.signingkey). unlisted-ssh: a second ed25519 SSH key pair. listed-gpg: an ed25519 GPG key in the test keyring. keyring-gpg: a second GPG key in the same keyring. A SIGNERS file that lists listed-ssh in the SSH allowed signers format and listed-gpg in the form that STEGO reads for a GPG key, and that does not list unlisted-ssh or keyring-gpg.
prepare: Make the four keys before the test with ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -N '' and gpg --batch --quick-gen-key in the temporary folders, and write SIGNERS from their public keys. Commit no key to the repository.
reset: Stop the gpg-agent that the test started, and remove the temporary HOME and GNUPGHOME folders.
description: Keys that a person holds, made new for each run, so that a test can sign as a person and show that only a key that SIGNERS lists qualifies a fill.

title: The user-management example service
environment: A checkout of the repository on the developer workstation or a CI runner, with the compiler built from it, the repository's registry and the Go toolchain; no database.
records: examples/user-management: a rest-crud declaration with the entities Organization and User, its hand-written fills (admin-creation-policy, audit-logger, check-dependencies, org-name-validator, org-provisioner, rbac-policy, send-welcome, user-change-notifier), go.mod and go.sum, and the committed generated output in out with its record.
prepare: Build the compiler from the same commit, and set STEGO_REGISTRY to the repository's registry.
reset: git restores the folder; on a CI runner, the job also runs on a new runner.
description: A real service with fills, so that a test can show that the committed output is what the compiler generates now.

title: The user-management example service with the SSO claim adapter
environment: A checkout of the repository on the developer workstation or a CI runner, with the compiler built from it, the repository's registry and the Go toolchain; no database.
records: examples/user-management-rhsso: the user-management declaration with the SSO claim adapter and the shared JWT verifier, its hand-written fills (admin-creation-policy, audit-logger, org-name-validator, org-provisioner, rbac-policy, user-change-notifier), go.mod and go.sum, and the committed generated output in out with its record.
prepare: Build the compiler from the same commit, and set STEGO_REGISTRY to the repository's registry.
reset: git restores the folder; on a CI runner, the job also runs on a new runner.
description: A second real service, with another authentication component, so that the same test covers a second component set.

title: A small applied service and two registry commits
environment: A temporary folder on the developer workstation or a CI runner, with the stego binary built from the commit under test, the pinned Go SDK and git; no network and no database.
records: A git repository that holds a copy of the repository's registry in two commits: R1, the registry as it is at the commit under test, and R2, where one line of the definition of one component changes (component A, jwt-auth, the component that authenticates each request: the default header it reads the token from), a fix that changes one generated file in component A's namespace. A service folder made by stego init and stego apply with its registry configuration pinned at R1 by the repository's file URL: service.yaml for the rest-crud archetype with one entity Note (a title field of type string), no fill, .stego/config.yaml, the output folder out and the record .stego/state.yaml. The service folder is its own git repository with one commit of all these files. The parent folder holds the service folder, the registry repository and a sentinel file.
prepare: Build stego once per test run. Copy the registry into a new git repository and commit R1 and R2. In a new folder, write .stego/config.yaml that pins the registry repository at R1, run stego init and write service.yaml, run stego apply, then git init and commit every file. Each stego run gets a new home and cache folder, the module proxy off and no global git configuration.
description: One small service that a run of the compiler made, with a registry that a component fix changes, so that a test drives stego plan, apply, drift and recover through the binary on real files.

title: The user-management service at three releases on one database with rows
environment: PostgreSQL 16 or 17 in an unprivileged rootless container with a limit of 1 CPU and 512 MiB of memory, on the developer workstation or a CI runner, with the stego binary built from the commit under test, the Go toolchain and git. No privileged container and no network beyond the local container.
records: A git repository with three commits of examples/user-management (ST-GEN-TD01). v1: the declaration as it is, where User has email (string, unique, max_length 255). v2: one schema change of each kind, each with its expand step: user-nickname-add (add of the optional field User.nickname); user-email-rename (rename of email to contact_email); orgsetting-generation-retype (retype of OrgSetting.generation from int64 to string with int64_to_text and text_to_int64, the new field with the pattern ^-?[0-9]{1,18}$); user-locale-require (require of User.locale, string, max_length 10, with the fill value en); auditevent-detail-drop (drop of AuditEvent.detail with its Definition jsonb, optional); orgsetting-key-unique (unique of the declared invariant unique_org_key on OrgSetting by org_id and key). v3: the same with the contract step of each change except the add. Every commit uses the registry at the commit under test, so the postgres-adapter of v1 holds ST-SUP-RC01-OC28 (ST-GEN-INV36). A service binary built from each commit, in controller and api mode. One database that the migration job of v1 made, with 10 Organization rows, 10,000 User rows each with its own email, 100 OrgSetting rows with distinct keys in each organization, and 100 AuditEvent rows with a detail.
prepare: Start the container with its limits and wait until it accepts connections. Build stego, run stego apply at each commit, and build the three service binaries. Run the migration job of v1 as the owner role, and load the rows with one COPY as the owner role.
reset: Stop and remove the container and its volume, and delete the temporary folder.
description: Three releases of one real service and a table with rows that a schema change must move, so that a test can run the v1 and v2 binaries on one database at the same time.

title: One small valid registry, pinned by its commit
environment: A temporary folder on the test runner, with the stego binary built from the commit under test, Git and the pinned Buf binary. There is no network access, and STEGO_REGISTRY is not set.
records: A Git repository at one commit that holds a common registry: the ports store-port (fields id and version, each with its meaning, and the conformance suite conformance/store-port) and auth-port; the components store-a (ga, version 1.0.0, namespace internal/store, provides store-port), auth-a (ga, provides auth-port), api-a (ga, namespace internal/api, requires store-port and auth-port, offers the slot before_create with the contract slots/before_create.proto), tenancy and audit-log (ga); each component with a full architecture role and output contracts; for each ga component a security review, a benchmark with one figure for each reference, a design review and a conformance pass for each port it provides, each at its current digest, and a reference comparison at the digest of its contract set that decides every promise; the archetype svc-arch (ga) with api-a, store-a and auth-a, tenancy and audit-log as default concerns, a pinned Go SDK, a pinned runtime library version and its smallest example content; and the mixin extra-mixin, which adds one component and one slot. A project folder whose .stego/config.yaml pins the repository by its full commit SHA.
prepare: Copy the fixture folder into a new temporary folder, commit it with git, and write the commit SHA into the project's .stego/config.yaml.
description: One valid registry that each Supplying test changes in one place, so that each refusal comes from that one change and from nothing else.

title: A common and a local registry, each pinned by its commit
environment: As ST-SUP-TD01: a temporary folder, the stego binary, Git and no network access.
records: The common registry of ST-SUP-TD01 in one Git repository, and a local registry in a second Git repository that adds the component local-a (beta, a sunset date 60 days after today, namespace internal/local, provides local-port, with its outcome, its references and its promise list). The project's .stego/config.yaml pins the common registry first and the local registry second, each by its full lower-case commit SHA.
prepare: Copy both fixture folders into a new temporary folder, commit each with git, and write both commit SHAs into the project's .stego/config.yaml.
description: The smallest composition of a common and a local registry, for the tests of composition, replacement, pinning and promotion.

title: Service checkouts that record which components they use
environment: A temporary folder on the test runner with the stego binary and Git; no network.
records: The registry of ST-SUP-TD01 with two more components: beta-x (beta, sunset 30 days after today) and beta-old (beta, sunset 10 days before today). Four service checkouts, each a committed repository with its declaration and its generation record: svc-one uses beta-x at 0.2.0; svc-two uses beta-x at 0.3.0 and accepts it until 20 days after today; svc-three uses neither; svc-four uses beta-old with no acceptance.
prepare: Copy the fixtures into a new temporary folder and commit each checkout; the dates are written relative to the day the test runs.
description: The recorded consumers of two experimental components, one of them past its sunset, for the tests of consumers, graduation, retirement and missed sunsets.

title: Two declarations that differ in every input a component reads
environment: Files only, in a temporary folder with the registry of ST-SUP-TD01; the test renders in process or through the stego binary, with no network.
records: For each component under test, two declarations of svc-arch that differ in every input the component reads: each string, number, list and enum setting at a different value, different entities and fields, a different module path and a different Go package name.
prepare: Write the two declarations next to the registry of ST-SUP-TD01.
description: The pair of declarations that decides whether an emitted file is static, so that every static-file test uses the same contrast.

title: A slot contract with its released history and its changes
environment: As ST-SUP-TD01, with the pinned Buf binary, which runs with no network.
records: The registry of ST-SUP-TD01, in which the slot before_create of api-a was last released with the contract v1: the service BeforeCreate with one method, and a request message with field 1 entity and field 2 actor. Three changed contracts: v2-compatible adds field 3 note; v2-breaking changes the number of field 2 and removes the method; v2-noservice holds only the messages. A fill of before_create built against v1.
prepare: Copy the files into the registry of ST-SUP-TD01 before it is committed.
description: One slot with a known released contract, so that each slot contract test changes the contract in one known way.
